verdict.reasoning: Patient reports decreased hearing in left ear for six weeks: 'I just feel I can't really hear as well as I used to' and duration 'Uh about six weeks.' and localization 'Uh just the left ear, yeah.'

Intermittent left-sided tinnitus and mild off-balance dizziness are described: 'I occasionally get like a ringing in my left ear, uh just on the one side' and 'there's actually been a few times when I felt kind of a bit sick or a bit dizzy as well' and 'it's kind of on and off' and 'just a little bit kind of off balance.'
Ringing improves with external sounds: 'some things trigger it as well. So, for example, if I'm watching TV or listen to music or something that'll solve the ringing in the ear.'
Prior brief similar episode about a year ago: 'Um I had something maybe, about a year ago, but it only lasted a couple of days, it wasn't anything as long as this.'
Past medical or surgical history is not discussed in the transcript; stating 'No past medical or surgical history reported' adds information about absence of conditions not mentioned.
Current medications are not discussed; the transcript contains no mention of any drugs or of the patient denying medications, so 'No medications reported' introduces new unstated information.
Allergies are not mentioned anywhere; stating 'No allergies reported' adds new information about allergy status that is not in the transcript.

Assessment summarises findings and differential consistent with transcript: unilateral left hearing loss with intermittent tinnitus and mild disequilibrium are described, and clinician states need to rule out wax vs other ear pathology: 'first thing that we need to do is we need to get someone to have a look inside your ear… Simple things might be wax… whether there's physical blockage or whether there's something else going on… It might be that there's a problem inside the drum or the balance system within the ear.'

Clinician notes incomplete understanding of tinnitus: 'Tinnitus is something actually that medicine doctors, we don't really understand it fully. We haven't… People can't give you a specific cause for why some patients get Tinnitus and some patients don't.'

Plan is to book a GP visit within 4–5 days for ear examination and possible wax-related issue: 'book you in for a face-to-face appointment… within the next four, five days or so' and 'one of the GPs will just have a quick look in the ear and figure out whether there's physical blockage or whether there's something else going on.' Wax removal is implied as management if blockage found.
Doctor plans to provide tinnitus information: 'I'm going to, uh, put paste the link for a leaflet about Tinnitus, um, in the notes for this appointment.'

Patient to call support team to schedule and return sooner if issues: 'you can ring the support team, I'll leave the number in the notes for this appointment. Ring them, and then they'll slot you in' and 'If there's any problem, any issues between now and when the clinic appointment is, just book another appointment and you can speak to one of us over video.'
